notes: THROUGHPUT TIER, NOT A QUALITY TIER. Same base weights, same 832x480 canvas,
same VRAM and the same amount of motion as otr_8gb_wan -- about 2.7x sooner.
The four-arm bench measured arm A and arm C at an identical peak delta
(6563.1 / 6531.1 / 6563.1 MiB at 17 / 49 / 81 frames) because step count does
not change peak activation. Choose this to render more clips per hour, not to
get better or longer clips.
max_render_frames is 17 DELIBERATELY. The 81-frame bench cell is a bench-graph
measurement and a bench cell never qualifies an engine (CLAUDE.md s0A). This
cap moves only after a canonical-workflow render proves the higher rung with
RESULT SUCCESS + obs_publish OK.
The canvas is ALSO declared on the adapter (render_canvas = (832, 480)), which
is what actually binds. The launch.env line here agrees with it and is a DRIFT
GUARD, not the authority: launch.env applies to the server process, so a leg
submitted to an already-booted server never sees it (PBUG-20260723-02).
OTR_FASTWAN_8GB_MAX_FRAMES is this engine's OWN ceiling key. It deliberately
does not read OTR_WAN_TI2V_MAX_FRAMES: one key for two tiers would let the WAN
tier's ceiling silently cap an engine that never opted into it.
LICENCE: the loaded LoRA is a Kijai extraction from a repo carrying NO
repo-level licence file. FastVideo and the Wan base both declare apache-2.0,
but that notice gap is unresolved, so the adapter ships commercial_clean=false.
Resolve the notice chain before treating output as commercially clear.
